NOTE:  PUBLIC PARTICIPATION INFORMATION
  Pursuant to the Governor's Executive Order N-29-20 and current State and County Public Health Orders,
  City Council Members will be participating via teleconference.

  - City Council meetings are recorded and live-streamed on the City’s website at www.rhe.city and
  available for viewing thereafter, and televised on Cox 33 and Frontier FiOS 38 on Wednesday and Friday
  following the meeting.

  - Members of the public may listen to the meeting live by calling: (1-669-900-6833) from any phone,
  Meeting ID: 826 0109 7074 , Meeting Password: 066081. (Please note you will not have the ability to
  speak using the call-in option from a phone line.)

  - Public correspondence may be emailed to the City Clerk at cityclerk@rollinghillsestatesca.gov. Emails
  received before 3:00 p.m. the night of the Council meeting will be forwarded to the City Council for their
  consideration and included as part of the record.

  - Members of the public may comment online using eComment on the “Meeting Agendas, Minutes &
  Videos” page of the City’s website (www.rhe.city/MeetingAgendas). Once the agenda is published, there
  will be an “eComment” button next to the linked agenda under "Upcoming Events". Follow this link to
  the City’s SpeakUp page. After you register, you may comment on any item on that particular agenda.
  These comments can be seen by the public, will be considered by the Council and become part of the
  record.

  - Members of the public who wish to speak during this meeting may join the Zoom meeting by accessing the
  Zoom app from a computer (downloaded at Zoom.com) or tablet or phone (downloaded in the App Store),
  by entering the following credentials: Meeting ID: 826 0109 7074 , Meeting Password: 066081. Members
  of the public who join the Zoom meeting will not have video, and may request to speak using the following
  process: After joining the Zoom meeting, if you wish to speak, please select the "raise hand" option at the
  lower portion of your screen. The City Clerk will send you a chat message to identify which item on the
  agenda you would like to speak on and will unmute your mic at the appropriate time.

  Agenda reports and other disclosable public records relating to each Open Session agenda item are
  available on the City's website under Meeting Agendas, Minutes & Videos at www.rhe.city.

MINUTES
  CITY COUNCIL MEETING
  JUNE 22, 2021

1.  CALL MEETING TO ORDER

A regular meeting of the City Council of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was called to order
by MAYOR ZUCKERMAN at 7:01 p.m. via teleconference, pursuant to the Governor’s
Executive Order N-29-20 and current State and County Public Health Orders.

2.  SALUTE TO THE FLAG

Flag salute led by MAYOR ZUCKERMAN.

3.  ROLL CALL

City Council Members Present:  Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan and Zuckerman

City Council Members Absent:  Huff

City Staff Present:  City Manager Greg Grammer
  Assistant City Manager Alexa Davis
  City Attorney Don Davis
  Administrative Services Director Michael Whitehead
  Planning Manager Jeannie Naughton
  Community Development & PW Director David Wahba
  Interim City Clerk Carrie Gallagher

4.  CEREMONIAL ITEMS

NONE.

5.  CONSENT CALENDAR

The following routine matters will be acted upon by one vote to approve with the majority
consent of the City Council. There will be no separate discussion of these items unless good
cause is shown by a member prior to the roll call vote. (Items removed for individual
consideration will be voted on separately.)

  COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ moved, seconded by MAYOR PRO TEM

  THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

NONE.

7.  PUBLIC HEARINGS

A.  FY 2021-22 BUDGET PUBLIC HEARING AND ADOPTION

City Manager Grammer introduced the item and Administrative Services Director Whitehead
provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

  COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ moved, seconded by, MAYOR ZUCKERMAN TO
  OPEN THE PUBLIC HEARING AT 7:09 P.M.

COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ thanked staff for producing a well done budget, noting creative
grant opportunities as an example of ways to ensure a very prudent and healthy budget. She
thanked COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA for her work on the Budget subcommittee.

MAYOR PRO TEM ZERUNYAN concurred with COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ’s comments,
and thanked Administrative Services Director Whitehead for his receptiveness and quick
responses to questions he had during the process.

COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA thanked Administrative Services Director Whitehead for
presenting a transparent and easy to understand budget.

MAYOR ZUCKERMAN also thanked COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA for her work on the
Budget subcommittee. He encouraged members of the public to review the budget online on
the City’s website. He added that the City anticipates receiving American Rescue Plan Act
(ARPA) funds later this year, allowing for an opportunity to utilize additional funds.

Public comment was invited via email, via eComment on the City’s website, and during the live
Zoom Webinar as noticed on the Agenda and on the City’s website and social media platforms.
No public testimony was received.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  3
JUNE 22, 2021
   COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA moved, seconded by, COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ
  TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  ADOPT RESOLUTION NO. 2485 AMENDING THE CITY’S PERSONNEL
  RULES.

  AYES:  Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan and Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  Huff

8.  NEW BUSINESS

A.  PERSONNEL RESOLUTIONS FY 2021-22

Assistant City Manager Davis presented the staff report (as per the agenda material)

  COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ moved, seconded by, MAYOR ZUCKERMAN TO
  APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  ADOPT RESOLUTION NO. 2481, A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL
  OF THE CITY OF ROLLING HILLS ESTATES APPROVING THE
  MEMORANDUM OF UNDERSTANDING SETTING BENEFITS, THE
  NUMBER OF AUTHORIZED POSITIONS AND COMPENSATION FOR THE
  CLASSIFIED EMPLOYEE GROUP IN THE CITY SERVICE.

  AYES:  Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan and Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  Huff

COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA questioned the wording in section 3A of Resolution 2482,
regarding the base pay increase description. Assistant City Manager Davis explained that the
base pay rate increase of 1% would be given to those with the measurement of “meets
expectations.”

MAYOR PRO TEM ZERUNYAN inquired if section 3A is currently written in a way to allow the
base pay rate increase to be given at the discretion of the City Manager. Assistant City
Manager Davis explained that is no longer the case, and any staff who meets each of the
outlined measurements of merit would receive the designated increase.

COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA proposed section 3A of Resolution 2482 and 2483 read “A
base pay rate increase of 1% with an overall rating of ‘Meets Expectations,’” which would be
consistent with 3B & 3C.

City Attorney Davis agreed with COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA’s suggested clarification.

Public comment was invited via email, via eComment on the City’s website, and during the live
Zoom Webinar as noticed on the Agenda and on the City’s website and social media platforms.
No public testimony was received.

  COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA moved, seconded by, COUNCIL MEMBER
  SCHMITZ TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  ADOPT RESOLUTION NO. 2482, A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL
  OF THE CITY OF ROLLING HILLS ESTATES ESTABLISHING THE NUMBER
  OF AUTHORIZED POSITIONS AND COMPENSATION FOR PROFESSIONAL
  CLASSIFICATIONS, AS AMENDED FOR SECTION 3A TO READ “A BASE
  PAY RATE INCREASE OF 1% WITH AN OVERALL RATING OF ‘MEETS
  EXPECTATIONS’”.

  AYES:  Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan and Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  Huff

Interim City Clerk Gallagher read Resolution 2482 by title.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  4
JUNE 22, 2021
   COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA moved, seconded by, COUNCIL MEMBER
  SCHMITZ TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  ADOPT RESOLUTION NO. 2483, A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL
  OF THE CITY OF ROLLING HILLS ESTATES ESTABLISHING THE
  NUMBER OF AUTHORIZED POSITIONS AND COMPENSATION FOR
  MANAGEMENT CLASSIFICATIONS, AS AMENDED FOR SECTION 3A TO
  READ “A BASE PAY RATE INCREASE OF 1% WITH AN OVERALL RATING
  OF ‘MEETS EXPECTATIONS’”.

  AYES:  Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan and Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  Huff

  COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ moved, seconded by, MAYOR PRO TEM
  ZERUNYAN TO ADOPT RESOLUTION NO. 2484, A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY
  COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF ROLLING HILLS ESTATES ESTABLISHING THE
  COMPENSATION OF POSITIONS IN THE PART-TIME EMPLOYEE GROUP.

  AYES:  Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan and Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  Huff

B.  MCGOWAN CONSULTING LLC PROFESSIONAL SERVICES AGREEMENT
  (AMENDMENT NO. 3) FOR MS4 PERMIT CONSULTING SERVICES

Community Development and Public Works Director Wahba provided a staff report (as per
the agenda material).

Susan Robinson of McGowan Consulting was present to answer Council questions.

COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ thanked Kathleen McGowan of McGowan Consulting for her
services.

COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA stated that she was in favor of a multiyear contract.

Ms. Robinson noted that although some changes will occur in the future, other items will drop
off resulting in a final budget that is not expected to change drastically, in response to COUNCIL
MEMBER STEGURA.

COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA also noted for the record that some of the items under the
scope of work are expenses shared with other cities.

MAYOR ZUCKERMAN asked for an update on the Torrance Airport Project. Ms. Robinson
added that the project is still in play and, while the application for funding has been pulled to
make way for funding other projects at this time, it is expected to be resubmitted by the end of
July.

Public comment was invited via email, via eComment on the City’s website, and during the live
Zoom Webinar as noticed on the Agenda and on the City’s website and social media platforms.
No public testimony was received.

  COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ moved, seconded by, COUNCIL MEMBER
  STEGURA TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  APPROVE AMENDMENT NO. 3 TO THE 2018 PROFESSIONAL SERVICES
  AGREEMENT WITH MCGOWAN CONSULTING LLC FOR MS4 PERMIT
  COMPLIANCE ASSISTANCE FOR FY 2021-22 IN AN AMOUNT NOT TO
  EXCEED $99,469.

  AYES:  Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan and Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  Huff

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  5
JUNE 22, 2021
 C.  PROJECT LIST FOR SB 1 FUND ELIGIBILITY (RESOLUTION No. 2480)

Community Development and Public Works Director Wahba provided a staff report (as per the
agenda material).

MAYOR PRO TEM ZERUNYAN, inquired if the street resurfacing project could start sooner
than expected. Community Development and Public Works Director Wahba explained there
is a significant amount of design work needed to be completed prior to starting the project. He
added that the City of Rancho Palos Verdes has its portion of Silver Spur Road included in
their capital budget but if for some reason RPV decides not to participate, RHE will move
forward with the balance of the project.

COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA inquired on the anticipated costs and asked if they are
expected to increase. Community Development and Public Works Director Wahba explained
that costs of material have drastically increased which could possibly increase the overall cost
of the project by $100,000 - $200,000. COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA expressed concern in
approving a project that could drastically increase in costs. Director Wahba replied that that
additional funds could be allocated from budget reserves or the project could be scaled back.

Public comment was invited via email, via eComment on the City’s website, and during the live
Zoom Webinar as noticed on the Agenda and on the City’s website and social media platforms.
No public testimony was received.

  COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA moved, seconded by, COUNCIL MEMBER
  SCHMITZ TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  APPROVE RESOLUTION NO. 2480, ADOPTING A LIST OF PROJECTS FOR
  FISCAL YEAR 2021-22 FUNDED BY SB 1, THE ROAD REPAIR AND
  ACCOUNTABILITY ACT OF 2017.

  AYES:  Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan and Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  Huff

Interim City Clerk Gallagher read Resolution 2482 by title.

9.  OLD BUSINESS

A.  UPDATE ON LOS ANGELES COUNTY SAFER AT HOME ORDER, CAL/OSHA
  WORKPLACE REQUIREMENTS AND STATUS OF CITY EVENTS (VERBAL
  REPORT)

City Manager Grammer reported that California’s economy reopened June 15 and two days
later Cal/OSHA announced that the same CDC guidelines would also pertain to fully
vaccinated employees who will no longer be required to wear masks in the workplace or
abide by social distancing requirements. City Hall employees and visitors who are fully
vaccinated are no longer required to wear masks but those who wish to may continue to do
so. Members of the public will be on an honor system, and will not be asked for proof of
vaccination.

Assistant City Manager Davis reported that the summer swim program kicked off today, after
being closed last year due to COVID-19 restrictions. She stated that the City partners with
the YMCA, Rancho Palos Verdes and the School District and that the MOU expires in 2024,
with an opportunity to extend the program an extra year due to last year’s cancellation.

Assistant City Manager Davis stated that a family movie “The Croods” is scheduled to be
shown at the City’s first Summer Movie Night this upcoming Saturday. She added that the
usual drive-in event will be replaced with a picnic-style event to include food vendors on site.
Additional Summer Movie Nights will be held in July and August. The annual Mayor's
Breakfast Ride is scheduled for July 10, and she reminded the Council to notify staff if they
wish to reserve a horse for the event. She added that a grab and go breakfast will replace
the traditional pancake breakfast. She also reported that the annual Hills are Alive Race is
scheduled for August 7, and due to COVID restrictions the Botanic Garden trail cannot be
utilized however alternatives are being considered. She added that a virtual race will be
added this year to accommodate those who are unable to make the event in person.
Although a date has not yet been determined, she reported that the Tracy Austin Event is
expected to be scheduled in the fall. The City Celebration event is tentatively scheduled for
September 25.

Assistant City Manager Davis concluded by adding that staff is looking to hold a concert in
the park event at the request of the Park & Activities Commission.
